skill.name: requirements-elicitation
skill.description: Guides structured requirements elicitation for software projects through stakeholder questions, requirement categories, prioritization, gap analysis, validation, and output formats.
skill.summary: Guide stakeholder interviews and convert answers into clear, testable software requirements.
skill.author: DoubleslashSE

content.value_statement: Requirements work often stalls when stakeholder input is vague or incomplete. This skill provides interview structures, question prompts, and validation methods for usable requirements.
actual_capabilities: Provides structured interview techniques for gathering stakeholder needs.
Separates functional requirements, non-functional requirements, constraints, and assumptions.
Uses MoSCoW and value versus effort methods for prioritization.
Supports gap analysis between current and desired system states.
Defines output formats for requirement lists, user stories, and traceability.
Offers role-based and scenario-based question templates.
limitations: Does not replace direct stakeholder validation or domain expert review.
Does not generate legally binding specifications without human approval.
Does not inspect live systems unless the user provides documents or access.
Does not estimate delivery timelines beyond supplied project context.

use_cases.title: Run Stakeholder Interviews
use_cases.description: Prepare focused questions for business owners, users, technical teams, operations, and external stakeholders.

use_cases.title: Shape MVP Scope
use_cases.description: Separate must-have launch needs from future enhancements using scope, value, effort, and assumption checks.

use_cases.title: Clarify Delivery Requirements
use_cases.description: Convert discovery notes into user stories, acceptance criteria, and traceable requirements for implementation planning.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Requirements Interview
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner discovery for a new project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me prepare questions for a new software project. The product idea is [summary]. Ask about users, goals, scope, and success criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Classify Stakeholder Notes
prompt_templates.scenario: Organize raw interview notes into requirement categories.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these stakeholder notes: [notes]. Group findings into functional requirements, non-functional requirements, constraints, assumptions, and open questions.

prompt_templates.title: Find Requirement Gaps
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare current and desired states before planning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare our current state [current] with desired state [desired]. Identify gaps, missing stakeholders, risky assumptions, and follow-up questions.

prompt_templates.title: Build Traceable Requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this discovery material into prioritized requirements with business objectives, user stories, acceptance criteria, validation checks, and traceability links: [material].

output_examples.input: Stakeholder says checkout must be faster and support guest purchases.
output: Functional requirement: Customers can complete checkout without creating an account.
Non-functional requirement: Checkout response time target needs a measurable threshold.
Follow-up question: What checkout duration is acceptable for the main customer segment?

output_examples.input: Team wants to replace an internal reporting tool but has unclear scope.
output: Current state: Reporting depends on manual spreadsheet updates.
Desired state: Users can generate approved reports from trusted system data.
Gap: Ownership, source systems, retention rules, and rollout timing need confirmation.

output_examples.input: Product manager has a backlog with mixed priorities.
output: Must have: Items needed for launch or compliance.
Should have: Items with strong value but manageable delay impact.
Could have: Items that improve experience but do not block core outcomes.

best_practices: Start with open questions, then narrow details through role-specific follow-up.
Validate each requirement for clarity, measurability, traceability, and testability.
Record assumptions and open questions beside the related requirement.
anti_patterns: Do not treat vague stakeholder preferences as confirmed requirements.
Do not skip non-functional needs such as security, performance, reliability, and supportability.
Do not prioritize features without business value, effort, and risk context.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps gather, organize, prioritize, and validate software requirements from stakeholders and existing documents.

faq.question: Can it create user stories?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure user stories with roles, capabilities, business value, and acceptance criteria.

faq.question: Does it cover non-functional requirements?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes prompts for security, usability, reliability, performance, supportability, and constraints.

faq.question: Can it support existing system replacement?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes brownfield questions for current state, change drivers, migration, rollback, and integrations.

faq.question: Does it make final project decisions?
faq.answer: No. It structures analysis and recommendations, but stakeholders must approve scope, priority, and acceptance criteria.

faq.question: How should I prepare inputs?
faq.answer: Provide project goals, stakeholder roles, current process notes, known constraints, and any existing requirement documents.
